_comment: Meter definitions for check T3.1 (docs/QUALITY_CHECKS.md). Varṇa-vṛtta patterns are per pāda, L = laghu, G = guru; the last syllable of a pāda is free (pādānta). Patterns drafted from the standard gaṇa definitions (Vṛttaratnākara); a human should confirm each against a printed source before relying on it. We keep our own list because tool meter tables can differ (Vidyut 0.4 lists pañcacāmara with 12 syllables; the classical definition ja-ra-ja-ra-ja-ga has 16).

pancacamara.name: pañcacāmara
pancacamara.ganas: ja ra ja ra ja ga

upajati.name: upajāti
upajati.note: Each pāda is indravajrā or upendravajrā.

vasantatilaka.name: vasantatilakā
vasantatilaka.ganas: ta bha ja ja ga ga

vasantatilaka-refrain.name: vasantatilakā (with an 11-syllable refrain)
vasantatilaka-refrain.note: Three vasantatilakā pādas and a closing refrain pāda of 11 syllables in indravajrā (Śivapañcākṣara v2: the refrain तस्मै मकाराय नमः शिवाय keeps the hymn's shared refrain, so the verse leaves vasantatilakā in its last pāda).

shikharini.name: śikhariṇī
shikharini.ganas: ya ma na sa bha la ga

mandakranta.name: mandākrāntā
mandakranta.ganas: ma bha na ta ta ga ga

shardulavikridita.name: śārdūlavikrīḍita
shardulavikridita.ganas: ma sa ja sa ta ta ga

sragdhara.name: sragdharā
sragdhara.ganas: ma ra bha na ya ya ya

anushtubh.name: anuṣṭubh (pathyā)
anushtubh.note: Per pāda: 8 syllables; 5th laghu, 6th guru in every pāda; 7th guru in odd pādas and laghu in even pādas. Vipulā variants are reported as warnings, not failures.

tunaka.name: tūṇaka
tunaka.note: 15 syllables, strict guru-laghu alternation (Kālabhairavāṣṭakam). Often mislabelled pañcacāmara online (that is 16, starting laghu). Name not yet confirmed against a printed prosody.
